# Calculate after you understand

The [one-file Python lab](linear_algebra_lab.py) checks exactly the small numbers in the lessons: vector addition and dot products, the tablet-to-wall transformation, matrix multiplication, determinant, linear systems, projection, Gram–Schmidt, a rotation, least squares, graph walks, Markov transitions and norm preservation.

From the repository root:

~~~bash
python3 mathematics/linear-algebra/examples/linear_algebra_lab.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s mathematics/linear-algebra/examples -p 'test_*.py'
~~~

These are **checks**, not demonstrations that every theorem is true. The actual justification is in each lesson's explanation of why the formula holds. Using a full linear algebra library would obscure the small calculations at this stage.

No dependencies beyond Python's standard library are needed.
